source: declarations of the published release assets, read and printed with the TypeScript compiler API by scripts/package-surface.mjs --write

..FENCE_COLS: the provenance columns as SQL text, for FencedBatch's text statements, which are deleted: a tree statement assigns provenance as nodes, with FENCE_ASSIGNMENTS, stampValue and nowValue
..FENCE_SET: the provenance assignment as SQL text, for FencedBatch's text statements, which are deleted: a tree statement assigns provenance as nodes, with FENCE_ASSIGNMENTS, stampValue and nowValue
..FENCE_VALS: the provenance values as SQL text, for FencedBatch's text statements, which are deleted: a tree statement assigns provenance as nodes, with FENCE_ASSIGNMENTS, stampValue and nowValue
..fenceSetAt: the preserved-instant provenance assignment as SQL text, deleted with FencedBatch's text statements: a tree statement copies the preserved instant as a column node

..NEXT_WAKE_SQL: the next-wake read as SQL text, exported so the query-plan suite could pin it: the read is a statement tree (nextWakeRead in @durablerun/core) sent as a batch of reads, and the suite records the statement a real nextWakeAtEpochMs sends
..SWEEP_SCAN_CANCELS_SQL: the sweep's due-cancellation scan as SQL text, exported so the query-plan suite could pin it: the read is a statement tree (sweepDueCancelsRead in @durablerun/core) sent as a batch of reads, and the suite records the statement a real sweep sends
..SWEEP_SCAN_EXPIRED_SQL: the sweep's expired-claim scan as SQL text, exported so the query-plan suite could pin it: the read is a statement tree (sweepExpiredClaimsRead in @durablerun/core) sent as a batch of reads, and the suite records the statement a real sweep sends

Clock.reason: elapsedMs() was added (PR #35): the driver loop measures its waits on a monotonic reading, so a step of the host clock moves none of them. A consumer that implements Clock adds the method, for example from performance.now(); one that passes systemClock changes nothing.

DERIVED_WRITABLE_COLUMNS.reason: max_attempts joined the task columns a generated follow-on may write (PR #56): a rollback pass runs after the user budget is spent, and the batch that places one raises the budget to the pass's ordinal. A consumer that reads the list changes nothing.

EventTimeoutError.reason: TaskTimeoutError became a subclass (PR #49), so that one catch covers an event await and a child await: name widened from the literal to string, and the constructor takes an optional message. A consumer that catches the error or reads eventName changes nothing.

FencedBatch.reason: Statements are trees (PR #37), and the text path is deleted (PR #52): cas, casMany, followOn, tail and openTail are gone, and the constructor requires tree, the dialect that compiles a tree. A consumer builds each statement as a tree and adds it with casTree, casManyTree, followOnTree, tailTree or openTailTree. Reads joined as readTree and readPrepared, and run's second parameter was renamed (PR #57). lockEvent is gone: a statement's definition names the event it is serialized on, which DefinedStatement carries as eventLock, and the batch takes that lock (PR #68). A consumer that called lockEvent names the event as defineStatement's third argument. A generated follow-on may bind its queue (PR #49), a generated set value may be an expression as well as text (PR #43), and one that writes a task's state gives it as an expression (PR #68).

LeaseState.reason: A refused heartbeat names why (PR #32): the interface became a union, and a lease that is not held carries reason, cancelled or lease-lost. A consumer that reads held and remainingMs changes nothing; a store that answers a heartbeat returns the reason with a refusal.

SchedulerStore.reason: The port grew with the engine. PR #28 added claimedTaskName and deferLaunch and removed reschedule's wakeDisposition; PR #29 added retryTask; PR #49 added awaitTaskDone; PR #56 added failRollback and made fail answer FailOutcome; PR #79 made failRollback take the step and the failure of the rollback, FailedRollback, in place of the attempt record, which the store now names and counts; PR #25 named the wake and checkpoint shapes WakeSpec and CheckpointWrite, with the same members, and renamed heartbeat's last parameter. A consumer that calls a published store stops passing wakeDisposition and otherwise changes nothing. A consumer that implements the port adds the five methods, answers FailOutcome from fail, and takes a FailedRollback in failRollback.

SpawnOptions.reason: The optional childOf was added (PR #49): the parent and call site from which the store builds a child task's idempotency key. A consumer changes nothing; ctx.spawn sets it, and it is refused together with idempotencyKey.

SqlStatement.reason: The optional skipUnlessWrote was added (PR #49): the earlier statement of the batch that gates this one, so an executor that pays a round trip for each statement can leave out one that cannot match. A consumer changes nothing, and an executor may ignore the field.

SuspendSignal.reason: The wake and checkpoint shapes that were written inline are named WakeSpec and CheckpointWrite (PR #25). Their members are the same, so a consumer changes nothing.

SweptRun.reason: The rollback-started arm was added (PR #56): a sweep cap that decides a task's failure places a rollback pass when a registered step is owed its rollback. A consumer that switches over kind exhaustively adds the arm.

TaskResult.reason: The optional rollback was added (PR #56): how a saga's rollback ended. A consumer changes nothing.

Launcher.reason: launch takes an optional second argument, LaunchOptions, whose one field is an abort signal: the resident driver fires it when the launch deadline passes, and the HTTP launcher ends its request with it (PR #73). A consumer that calls launch changes nothing, and one that implements Launcher still compiles; it reads the signal to end a launch the driver has stopped waiting for.

SqlTransactionLock.reason: It gained the arm { kind: 'migration' }: a migration write carries the migration lock in the batch control as a lock coordinate, where the MySQL executor chose it from the batch label, and that executor refuses a migration write that names none (PR #83). A consumer that builds a transaction lock changes nothing, and one that switches over kind exhaustively adds the arm.

DriverLoopOptions.reason: The optional wakeFloorMs was added (PR #28): wake() calls inside the floor coalesce into one look. A consumer changes nothing.

createWakeServer.reason: The parameter narrowed to the one method the server calls, Pick<DriverLoop, 'wake'> (PR #25). A DriverLoop still fits, so a consumer changes nothing.

ReplayContext.reason: The worker's context class. Its constructor takes the decoded WorkerClaimedRun (PR #36) and a lease-end latch in place of the lease-lost AbortSignal, and the issuer's leaseLost became leaseEnded, which carries the reason (PR #32). spawn and awaitTask were added (PR #49). Step rollback added StepOptions, rollingBack, nextRollback, runRollback, rollbackFailure and the issuer's rollbackPhase (PR #56), and rollbackFailure and a halting nextRollback answer the failed rollback, FailedRollback, where they answered its attempt record (PR #79). A task function receives the context as TaskContext and changes nothing. A consumer that constructs a ReplayContext passes a latch object, and one that supplies its own issuer implements leaseEnded and rollbackPhase.

RunInvocation.reason: The interface became a pick of LaunchInvocation's four claim ids in place of a hand copy of them (PR #28). The members are the same, so a consumer changes nothing.

TaskContext.reason: spawn and awaitTask were added (PR #49), and step takes an optional third argument that registers a rollback (PR #56). A task function changes nothing; a consumer that implements TaskContext, a test double for example, adds the two methods.

WorkerOutcome.reason: New arms: cancelled (PR #28), incompatible-store (PR #36), and rolling-back, rolled-back and rollback-failed (PR #56). A consumer that switches over kind exhaustively adds the arms.

LibsqlExecutor.reason: The constructor takes an optional third argument, databaseUrl, the URL a client handed to it was created with (PR3.15): a file-backed executor fixes its database file from that URL, so that a connection it replaces after a failed batch reaches the same file, and a file-backed executor made without it never replaces a connection. A consumer that calls open(), or hands it a client with no fileBacked flag, changes nothing; one that hands it a file-backed client passes that client's URL too.

LibsqlSchedulerStore.reason: It implements SchedulerStore, and its public methods changed with the port, for the reasons under that name: claimedTaskName, deferLaunch, retryTask, awaitTaskDone and failRollback were added, fail answers FailOutcome, failRollback takes a FailedRollback (PR #79), and reschedule lost wakeDisposition. It extends HeldPort, the class in core that checks every string the port takes, where each store checked its own (PR #86). A consumer stops passing wakeDisposition and otherwise changes nothing.

openTestDb.reason: The optional url was added (PR #25), so a test can open a database it names. A consumer changes nothing.
